main_text.p: latroni, qui metum viatori incussit, & contra bonos mores extorsit ab eo juramentum iniquum, jus nullum accrescit, proinde nec qui juravit obligatur. Re-spondeo, exurgere posse à Juramento duplicem obligationem: unam homini qui juratur, ut parti; Deo per quem juratur alteram, ut testi & vindici. Multa pos-sunt impedire priorem illam obligatio-nem, ita ut jus nullum consequatur is cui juratur, nec ei quidquam in foro conscientiæ ex æquo bono à jurante debeatur: & de istoc obligationis & debiti genere procedit objectio. Verum cessante obligatione respectu hominis injuriam aut vim inferentis, manet tamen Deo facta obligatio: cui & irreverentia fit, si quis juramentum admittat non intendens implere; & injuria, si admissum insuper habeatur.
main_text.head: SECT. XVII.
main_text.p: Casus 31Restat unus adhuc Casus, huic loco peculiaris: si quis incidens in latrones cogatur, ne ab eis occidatur, juramenti silentium promittere; sc. nunquam ipsorum latrocinia cuiquam revelaturum aut nomina magistratui proditurum

page.notes: Right edge of the text block is cropped by the scan; a few letters at the line ends are cut off and were read from context. The catchword "Dif" is partly cut off, so it is marked [?]. The marginal note reads "Casus" with its long s printed as f; the "31" is printed beside it. The printed "ff" is read as "ss" in pos-sunt and insuper. Small marks at the left margin are specks and were left out.
